title: UNEP: Opportunity has ‘been lost’ to meet 1.5C warming limit without ‘overshoot’ - Carbon Brief
gist: UNEP's 2026 emissions gap report says a temporary breach of 1.5C is unavoidable, with the lowest-overshoot path peaking at 1.7-1.8C and requiring emissions cuts of 18% by 2030 and 45% by 2035 versus 2025, while current pledges deliver only 5-8% and 11-15%. Current policies point to 2.8C by 2100, and the report calls renewables the only area on track.

insights.claim: UNEP says a temporary breach of the Paris Agreement's 1.5C limit is now inevitable after decades of insufficient climate action, so the task is to minimise the size and duration of overshoot and establish a credible return path to 1.5C by the end of the century.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Official framing shifts from avoiding 1.5C to managing overshoot, raising reliance on carbon removal in policy and capital allocation.
